key: ‘The children of Israel shall pitch by their fathers’houses; every man with his own standard, according to the ensigns; a good way off shall they pitch round about the tent of meeting.
s: After the census, the LORD sets each tribe’s place, three to a standard on each side of the Tabernacle; Rashi, on 2:2, reads ‘the ensigns’ as cloths coloured like each tribe’s breastplate stone, and Ibn Ezra, on 2:2, as figures, by the ancients’ account a man, lion, ox and eagle, like the cherubim Ezekiel saw.
src: Rashi and Ibn Ezra, on Numbers 2:2, Hebrew (Rashi: Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934; Ibn Ezra: “On Your Way”), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.words: כָּל דֶּגֶל יִהְיֶה לוֹ אוֹת מַפָּה צְבוּעָה תְלוּיָה בוֹ, צִבְעוֹ שֶׁל זֶה לֹא כְצִבְעוֹ שֶׁל זֶה, צֶבַע כָּל אֶחָד כְּגוֹן אַבְנוֹ הַקְּבוּעָה בַחֹשֶׁן … סימנים היו בכל דגל ודגל וקדמונינו אמרו שהיה בדגל ראובן צורת אדם מכח דרש דודאים ובדגל יהודה צורת אריה כי בו המשילו יעקב ובדגל אפרים צורת שור מטעם בכור שור ובדגל דן צורת נשר עד שידמו לכרובים שראה יחזקאל הנביא
evidence.gloss: [Rashi, on 2:2, ‘with the signs’:] Each standard shall have a sign, a dyed cloth hanging on it, the colour of one unlike the colour of another, the colour of each like its stone set in the breastplate. … [Ibn Ezra, on 2:2:] There were signs on every standard, and our ancients said that on Reuben’s standard was the form of a man, from the homily on the mandrakes; on Judah’s the form of a lion, for Jacob likened him to one; on Ephraim’s the form of an ox, from ‘his firstling bullock’; and on Dan’s the form of an eagle; so that they resembled the cherubim that Ezekiel the prophet saw.

reason: The defect is real: day.js prints Numbers 2:2 as ‘fathers’houses’ (the same missing space recurs at 2:32 and 2:34 and in the app’s Tanakh text elsewhere; JPS 1917 prints ‘fathers’ houses’), and the verse opens the LORD’s speech whose quotation mark closes only at 2:31, as the JPS prints it. But rule 8 forbids mending the key, the repair belongs to the app’s text and so to the operator, and the reading cannot move to another verse: Rashi’s dyed cloths and Ibn Ezra’s figures are both comments on באתת in 2:2 alone, re-opened today (packet.js tanakh 42 --verse 2:2) and verbatim as the evidence gives them. Swapping in the standby (Sforno on 2:17) would replace a sound commentator and reading that the problem does not question. The entry stands unchanged; FOR THE OPERATOR: repair the systematic missing space after the apostrophe (fathers’ houses) in the app’s JPS text and rerun verse.js on this same key, or, if the text is not repaired before landing, ship the standby tanakh-02-d042-s once it is verified.
